blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — duration of Transmission-Based Precautions
stem: A client is receiving Droplet Precautions for a respiratory infection. How should the nurse determine when the precautions can be discontinued?

options.A: Use the organism- and condition-specific duration criteria in current infection-control guidance because required duration varies by infection.
options.B: Discontinue Droplet Precautions 24 hours after they begin whenever the client is clinically improving, regardless of the identified infection.
options.C: Continue Droplet Precautions through the entire hospitalization because pathogen-specific discontinuation criteria are not used in healthcare settings.
options.D: Discontinue Droplet Precautions when the client requests it if symptoms have improved, even when the recommended transmission-risk period remains.

rationale: A is correct. CDC Appendix A provides infection- and condition-specific types and durations of precautions. Durations vary substantially: some conditions use a defined interval after effective therapy, others continue for the duration of illness, and others use laboratory or case-specific criteria. B applies a universal 24-hour rule that does not exist. C incorrectly makes precautions indefinite for the hospitalization. D bases discontinuation on preference rather than transmission-risk criteria.
educational_objective: Use pathogen- and condition-specific CDC criteria to determine the duration of Transmission-Based Precautions rather than applying a universal stopping time.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Appendix A: Type and Duration of Precautions Recommended for Selected Infections and Conditions; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC Appendix A dated February 7, 2025 and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC Appendix A lines 18-36 identify the type-and-duration table and updates. The table lists condition-specific durations, e.g., duration of illness, treatment/culture-based criteria, fixed age periods, or case-by-case criteria depending on the infection.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports pathogen/condition-specific discontinuation criteria and demonstrates that duration is not governed by one universal interval.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles and use appropriate transmission-prevention practices.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; the clinical key is supported by current CDC HTML.

option_audit.A: Correct; uses CDC's condition-specific duration criteria.
option_audit.B: Plausible treatment-response shortcut but incorrectly applies a universal 24-hour interval.
option_audit.C: Plausible overcautious approach but ignores pathogen-specific stopping criteria.
option_audit.D: Plausible patient-preference framing but does not address transmission risk.

cueing_audit.answer_length: Options are comparable in length and detail; the key is not uniquely signaled.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on simplistic always/never/only wording.
